title: Catch every crash: ingest macOS crash reports and detect unclean exits at launch
description: Paul: 'I clicked a feed follow and the app quit. We should catch all crashes.' The panic hook only sees Rust panics; a native crash (WKWebView, Lance/ONNX FFI, SIGSEGV/SIGABRT) leaves only a macOS .ips in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports, and a plain exit leaves nothing. At launch: (1) write a running stamp and clear it on clean shutdown; a stamp present at launch = unclean exit — record at error level with the previous version, uptime, and the last few log lines; (2) scan DiagnosticReports for new alchemy/Alchemy .ips since the last launch, parse exception type and the crashed thread's top frames, record them at fatal level and surface a quiet notice ('Alchemy crashed last time. The report is in the log.') with Reveal; (3) expose through recent_errors over IPC and MCP. Also record window-close vs quit so 'the app quit' is distinguishable.
close_reason: Merged to main: crashwatch.rs (running stamp → unclean-exit record; .ips ingestion at fatal, quiet; window-close vs quit; crash_notice + HealthBanner row; recent_errors over MCP)

title: Bundle writes ran a second Mac out of file descriptors

Fixed on main 9a92c2f: RLIMIT_NOFILE raised to OPEN_MAX at startup, two concurrent bundle writes, one retry after 15s.
close_reason: Fixed on main 9a92c2f

title: Bindings go stale when the other Mac moves the bundles; the writer recreates the old folder
description: Two-Mac 0.56.0: Mac A moved its bundles into the app container and iCloud carried the move to Mac B. Mac B's bindings still named the old iCloud Drive/Alchemy/<slug> paths (log: 'could not move ...: No such file or directory' x18), and the next write-through recreated those folders from Mac B's notebooks, so the old folder came back and the container gained -2 copies (alchemy-development-2). Fix: (1) the writer never creates a missing bundle root after bind/seed; a missing root marks the binding lost, logs once, and skips writes; (2) a lost binding rebinds automatically to a bundle under notebooks_dir (the container) whose alchemy.id matches, keeping the manifest; the root watcher and the move's per-notebook error path use the same rebind; (3) only if no bundle with that id exists anywhere does the app fall back to re-seeding, and then into notebooks_dir, never the old path.
close_reason: Merged to main 265cf78: two-sighting delete grace + outage stand-down, lost bindings rebind by alchemy.id and the writer never recreates a root, per-notebook move waits with a move guard, whole-folder move with id-before-name placement

title: OKF read-back deletes an entity the moment its file is absent
description: okf.rs 'A concept file that is gone takes its entity with it' fires on a single pass. During an iCloud/FileProvider sync a claimed file can be transiently absent (mid-move, mid-download). Fix: delete only when the file is absent on two consecutive passes at least 60 s apart, and skip the pass entirely (log it) when a large share of a bundle's claimed files vanish at once. Route 'deleted on disk' through diagnostics::record so it reaches the app log, not just stderr.
close_reason: Merged to main 265cf78: two-sighting delete grace + outage stand-down, lost bindings rebind by alchemy.id and the writer never recreates a root, per-notebook move waits with a move guard, whole-folder move with id-before-name placement

title: unbind_notebook_okf reports success but the binding is rewritten while the notebook is open
description:
## What

`unbind_notebook_okf` returns `{"notebookId": "...", "okfPath": null}` and the
binding stays in `okf-bindings.json` when the notebook's window is open (or a
write-through is still in flight). The caller is told the notebook was
unbound; it was not. The bundle keeps being written and the reconciler keeps
reading it back.

## Repro

Installed 0.55.0, MCP on 41414.

    open "alchemy://notebook/<id>"          # leave the window open
    unbind_notebook_okf(notebook_id="<id>")
    -> {"notebookId": "<id>", "okfPath": null}

    python3 -c 'import json,os; b=json.load(open(os.path.expanduser(
      "~/Library/Application Support/com.thrashr888.alchemy/okf-bindings.json")));
      print("<id>" in b)'
    -> True

`list_notebooks` also still reports the `okfPath`. Repeating the unbind five
times over two minutes did not clear it:

    10:43:46 BOUND 30
    10:44:06 BOUND 30
    ... (unchanged through 10:45:26)

The resurrected entry carries a fresh `lastWriteAt` (1788457384142, after the
unbind), so a write-through is saving the whole bindings map back from a copy
taken before the unbind.

Quitting the app does not clear it either — the entry is on disk. But in a
**fresh session with the notebook closed**, the same call sticks first time:

    after fresh-session unbind: unbound 29

## Ask

Have the unbind cancel/drain any pending write for that notebook before
clearing the entry, and have the writer re-read the bindings file rather than
persisting a stale in-memory map. Failing that, the command should return an
error instead of `okfPath: null` when the entry is still there afterwards.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.
close_reason: Fixed on main 991d35d (cld/okf-sync-fixes): adopted paths close the duplication loop, collision-safe placement, starter notebooks never bind + watcher decide_bundle + one-time heal, SF_DATALESS stub detection, per-file mtime reconcile, locked unbind, delete logging, bind mkdir

title: OKF log.md never records a deletion, though RFC-okf-live 5.3 says a vanished file's delete is logged
description:
## What

RFC-okf-live.md 5.3's read-back table says a concept file that is gone should
"delete the entity, log it". The delete happens; the log entry does not.

`okf.rs:2489` records the removal with `crate::note!` only, which is
stderr-only and never reaches `log.md` or
`~/Library/Logs/com.thrashr888.alchemy/alchemy.log`. `okf_log_append` is called
for writes and for conflict losers, not for deletions.

## Repro

Bind a notebook with two notes. Delete one note's file:

    rm "<bundle>/notes/<slug>-disposable-note.md"

Wait for the reconcile pass. The note is correctly removed from the app, and
`log.md` gains only write lines:

    # Log

    ## 2026-09-03 — thrashr888

    - 16:54:01Z 2 written — 1 sources, 1 notes. (alchemy/0.55.0)
    - 17:16:24Z 1 written — 1 sources, 2 notes. (alchemy/0.55.0)
    - 17:22:07Z 3 written, 1 moved — 1 sources, 3 notes. (alchemy/0.55.0)

Nothing names the deleted concept. On a shared folder the log is the only
record the other side has of why a concept disappeared, which is the reason
5.3 asks for the line in the first place.

## Ask

Append a dated `log.md` entry naming each deleted concept path in the same
pass that removes it, the way the conflict-loser entries already do.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.

title: OKF read-back latency is minutes, not the ~2s RFC-okf-live promises (open 36s, closed 228s to >10min)
description:
## What

RFC-okf-live.md 1 says a bound notebook and its bundle "agree within seconds,
in both directions", and 5.2/5.3 put the number at a two-second debounce with
FSEvents for open notebooks and a ten-minute sweep for closed ones. Measured
on installed 0.55.0, an outside edit to a note file takes:

| provider | notebook | outside-edit -> visible in app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dropbox | open | 36 s |
| OneDrive | closed | 228 s |
| Google Drive | closed | not within 630 s (gave up) |

Write-through is fine and well inside budget: seed pass 1.35 s (Dropbox),
0.40 s (Drive), 0.32 s (OneDrive); a new note reached all three bundles in
under 4 s.

## Repro

    # installed 0.55.0, three notebooks bound to folders under the three
    # cloud roots, one note each
    open "alchemy://notebook/<dropbox nb>"     # leave the other two closed
    # edit the body of each notes/<slug>.md with sed, note the time
    # poll get_note / list_notes over MCP until the new text appears

Earlier in the same session an outside edit to a **closed** notebook's note
was still not read back after 862 s of polling, and an edit with the notebook
**open** was not read back after 120 s — the pass that finally took both in
landed about five minutes later.

## Two things that look like the cause

1. **`reconcile_all` is a serial walk over every binding.** `scheduler.rs:588`
   calls it on the closed tick; `okf.rs:2686` loops `load_bindings()` and
   awaits `reconcile()` for each one in turn, reading every concept file of
   every bound bundle. This Mac has 26 bindings and one bundle alone
   (`meridian`) holds 742 sources, so a single pass is minutes of file I/O.
   Notebooks late in the map wait for everything before them — which matches
   Google Drive never landing while OneDrive landed at 228 s.

2. **The open-notebook FSEvents path needs a scheduler tick first.**
   `fswatch::rearm()` only adds a bound root when the notebook is in
   `open_notebook_ids()`, and rearm runs on the minute tick, so the 2 s
   debounce cannot start until up to a minute after the window opens. 36 s is
   consistent with that.

## Ask

Give the reconcile sweep concurrency or a per-notebook budget so one large
bundle cannot starve the rest, and rearm the watcher on window-open rather
than waiting for the next tick.

title: OKF write-through destroys a concept file on slug collision, leaving a dangling manifest entry and a broken index.md link
description:
## What

When a reconcile pass creates a new concept whose title slugs to a name an
existing concept already owns, the write pass writes the new file at the base
slug and then re-slugs the existing concept to `-2` — and the base-slug file
ends up gone. The result:

- one entity's file is missing from the bundle entirely,
- the manifest still claims that path,
- `index.md` links to a file that does not exist.

## Repro

Bind a notebook with a note titled "Dropbox test note". Drop a cloud-style
conflict copy beside it carrying the same `title:` in frontmatter:

    notes/dropbox-test-note.md                     (existing, entity 302d9255)
    notes/dropbox-test-note (conflicted copy).md   (new, same title)

After the reconcile + write pass, `log.md` says

    17:22:07Z 3 written, 1 moved — 1 sources, 3 notes. (alchemy/0.55.0)

and `notes/` holds

    dropbox-hand-added.md
    dropbox-test-note (conflicted copy).md
    dropbox-test-note-2.md          <- entity 302d9255 moved here
    hand-added.md
    index.md

`dropbox-test-note.md` is **gone**, but the manifest still has

    ca135368-14aa-4e78-b8c5-706ea52739f5 -> notes/dropbox-test-note.md

so entity ca135368 (the note created from the conflict copy) has no file at
all, and `index.md` still renders

    - [Dropbox test note](dropbox-test-note.md) — CONFLICT-MARKER ...

a dead link.

## Ordering

Looks like the new concept is written at the base slug first, then the
existing concept's rename to `-2` runs and the rename target/source ordering
clobbers it — or the prune step removes the base-slug file because the
manifest entry that claimed it had already been rewritten to `-2`.

## Not only a test artifact

The same shape shows on a real bundle: `~/Library/Mobile Documents/
com~apple~CloudDocs/Alchemy/meridian` has 77 note files on disk while its
manifest claims 85 note paths — 8 claimed files do not exist.

## Note

Closely related to the unbounded-duplication issue filed alongside this one;
both come from the writer choosing a new name instead of claiming the file the
reconciler actually read. Fixing the claim may fix both, but the missing-file
outcome is worth its own test.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.

title: OKF read-back duplicates without bound: any hand-added file under notes/ multiplies every reconcile pass
description:
## Severity

This is the worst thing found in the v0.55.0 cloud QA pass. A bound notebook
went from 3 notes to 55 notes in five minutes and was still accelerating when
I unbound it to stop it. It fills the store and the bundle folder without
limit, and the trigger is the exact workflow RFC-okf-live.md sells: an agent
or a person adding a markdown file to `notes/` by hand.

## The loop

1. Someone drops `notes/hand-added.md` into a bound bundle.
2. `reconcile()` classifies it `Create` (no manifest entry) and makes a note.
3. The write-through writes that note to **its own slug**,
   `notes/dropbox-hand-added.md`, and records *that* path in the manifest.
4. `hand-added.md` is never renamed, never deleted, and never claimed by the
   manifest. So on the next pass it is still unknown -> `Create` again.
5. Repeat forever. Each pass also re-imports the previous pass's leftovers.

Same loop for a cloud conflict copy: `notes/<name> (conflicted copy).md`
imports as a note (which is the intended "keep both" outcome per 5.6), gets
written out as `<slug>-2.md`, and the conflict-copy file itself stays orphaned
and re-imports on every pass.

## Repro

Installed 0.55.0, MCP on 127.0.0.1:41414.

    # bind a notebook with one note to an empty folder
    bind_notebook_okf(notebook_id, "<folder>")
    printf -- '---\ntype: Note\ntitle: "Hand added"\n---\n\nbody\n' > "<folder>/notes/hand-added.md"
    # wait for reconcile, then poll
    watch 'list_notes(notebook_id) | grep -c title; ls "<folder>/notes" | wc -l'

Observed (Dropbox folder, notebook open):

    10:35:57 notes_in_app=11 files_on_disk=12
    10:36:42 notes_in_app=19 files_on_disk=20
    10:37:27 notes_in_app=25 files_on_disk=28
    10:38:13 notes_in_app=35 files_on_disk=36
    10:38:58 notes_in_app=45 files_on_disk=46
    10:39:44 notes_in_app=55 files_on_disk=56

`notes/` filled with `dropbox-hand-added-2.md`, `-3.md`, `-4.md`, ...
Reproduced identically on the Google Drive bundle.

`unbind_notebook_okf` stops it; the notes already created stay.

## Fix direction

After taking a file in, the writer has to claim the file it read, not invent a
new name for it. Either record the incoming path in the manifest as that
entity's path (and leave the file where it is), or rename the incoming file to
the slug in the same pass. A `Create` whose entity is written to a different
path must never leave the source file unclaimed.

A cheap guard worth having regardless: refuse to create more than N concepts
from one reconcile pass and record a diagnostics error, so a loop like this
trips a circuit breaker instead of running until the disk fills.

## Blast radius on this Mac

Paul's 25 real bound bundles in iCloud are **not** currently looping - I
checked `meridian` (77 notes / 742 sources) and its notes have zero orphans.
The loop needs a file whose name does not match the writer's slug, which only
happens once somebody hand-adds or a cloud provider writes a conflict copy.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.

title: Two notebooks bound to one OKF bundle folder after a 0.55.0 first launch duplicated notebooks
description:
## What

On the first launch of the installed 0.55.0 build, the app created duplicate
notebooks and duplicate `-2` bundle folders in the Notebooks dir, and ended
with **two distinct notebook ids bound to the same bundle path**. That is two
binding ids, two manifests, and two writers over one folder, which
RFC-okf-live.md 5.6 says must never happen ("two writers must never fight over
one file").

## Evidence

`~/Library/Application Support/com.thrashr888.alchemy/okf-bindings.json`:

    2 x .../CloudDocs/Alchemy/458-spider-purchase-2
       notebook 3084257a-e35c-47f5-899c-90d1fb48630b  binding id 5042f715-c486-41a3-be73-8c2e3c171b61
       notebook e7d6f85a-15a5-4ddd-8fe7-fd6a2f95ab94  binding id 0d4d1b8b-db2a-4f9f-92bb-b0aa006f01a0

`list_notebooks` over MCP reports 44 notebooks with three duplicated titles:

    'Curated Supply: Well-Designed Objects': 3
    'AI Research: Landmark Papers': 3
    '458 Spider Purchase': 3

Two of those rows come back with the **same id repeated** (a23d2142-... and
4ae9d35f-... each appear twice in one `list_notebooks` response), which looks
like duplicate rows in the notebooks table rather than distinct notebooks.

Five new `-2` bundle folders appeared in
`~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Alchemy/` timestamped within
90 s of the 0.55.0 startup line:

    458-spider-purchase-2
    ai-research-landmark-papers-2
    curated-supply-well-designed-objects-2
    earnings-reports-for-top-50-corporations-2
    introduction-to-alchemy-2

`458-spider-purchase-2/index.md` carries `generated.by: alchemy/0.55.0` and
`at: 2026-09-03T16:50:25Z`; the app's startup line is 16:50:01Z. So the
0.55.0 launch wrote them.

Nothing was recorded in `~/Library/Logs/com.thrashr888.alchemy/alchemy.log` —
the last line is the 0.55.0 startup entry. The duplication was silent.

## Suspected path

`okf::open_found_bundles()` (called from `scheduler.rs:589` and
`fswatch.rs:241`) plus the `keep_on_disk` bind-at-creation pass. 5.7 says "a
bundle whose `alchemy.id` matches a notebook already bound elsewhere is the
same notebook and rebinds rather than duplicating" — that guard did not hold
here, or the duplicate notebook rows existed first and each got its own
slug-deduped folder.

## Confound, stated honestly

Thirty seconds before this launch, a stale **0.48.0** debug build in
`src-tauri/target/debug/bundle/` was launched by mistake (`open -a Alchemy`
resolves to it) and shared the same LanceDB data dir. 0.48.0 predates OKF
live entirely. It may have contributed to the duplicate rows, but it cannot
have written the `-2` OKF bundles, and it does not explain two live bindings
pointing at one folder.

## Ask

Regardless of how the duplicate notebooks arose, `bind_notebook_okf` and the
auto-bind paths should refuse (or rebind) when the target path is already
claimed by another notebook's binding, and `open_found_bundles` should not be
able to mint a second binding for a folder that already has one.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.
notes: Second cause: Paul's other Mac. Starter notebooks (examples.rs) have different ids per machine; each Mac bound its own copy and the other's root watcher imported it → 47 notebooks on Home, most twice. Rule added to the fix: starters never bind by default and the watcher never opens a starter's bundle; heal unbinds bound starters and archives '-2' imports; two-Mac rebind-by-alchemy.id.
close_reason: Fixed on main 991d35d (cld/okf-sync-fixes): adopted paths close the duplication loop, collision-safe placement, starter notebooks never bind + watcher decide_bundle + one-time heal, SF_DATALESS stub detection, per-file mtime reconcile, locked unbind, delete logging, bind mkdir

title: OKF stub detection is dead code on macOS 26+: iCloud evicts to a dataless file, not a .icloud dot-stub
description:
## What

Every OKF cloud-stub code path keys on the legacy `.name.icloud` dot-stub
naming. On macOS 26/27 (tested: 27.0, build 26A5421a) iCloud Drive no longer
creates dot-stubs. Evicting a file leaves the file **at its own path** with
`st_flags` carrying `dataless` and `st_blocks == 0`. No hidden sibling is
written.

Result: `okf::is_evicted_stub()` returns false for every evicted file on every
provider, including iCloud, so all of the following are inert:

- `okf.rs:2698 is_evicted_stub()` — `path.exists()` is TRUE for a dataless
  file, so it returns early with false before the sibling check.
- `okf.rs:2711 hydrate_if_evicted()` — never nudges.
- `okf.rs:2318 evicted_concepts()` — always returns an empty vec, so the
  `brctl download` batch in `reconcile()` (okf.rs:2400-2405) never fires.
- The writer's three "never overwrite a stub" guards:
  `settle_reference` (okf.rs:1743), `free_reference_name` (okf.rs:1772),
  `place_reference` (okf.rs:1828).
- `fswatch.rs:172` `is_scannable()`'s `.icloud` allowance.
- `hygiene.rs:145-149`'s stub check.

## Repro

    NB=$(alchemy/MCP create_notebook "Stub test")
    # add a note, then bind_notebook_okf to a folder in iCloud Drive
    brctl evict "<bundle>/notes/<slug>.md"
    stat -f "%N blocks=%b size=%z flags=%Sf" "<bundle>/notes/<slug>.md"

Observed on 27.0:

    ... blocks=0 size=327 flags=compressed,dataless

and `ls -a` on the directory shows **no** `.stub-victim-note.md.icloud`.
`test -f` on the real path succeeds.

Same shape for Dropbox and Google Drive (both FileProvider extensions under
`~/Library/CloudStorage`): a real user file there reads
`blocks=0 size=1354 flags=compressed,dataless`, with no dot-stub sibling.

## Why it matters

1. The "never overwrite a stub" guarantee in RFC-okf-live.md 5.6 is not
   enforced anywhere on current macOS.
2. `free_reference_name()` calls `std::fs::read(&at)` on a dataless
   `references/` file to compare hashes. That forces a synchronous, blocking
   full download of the original (up to the 50 MB cap) inside the write path.
3. The reconciler reads every concept file unconditionally, which materializes
   evicted concepts and silently undoes the user's "free up space" (see the
   companion issue on re-hydration).

## Fix direction

Detect datalessness portably instead of by filename. `st_flags & SF_DATALESS`
(0x40000000) is set by iCloud **and** by every FileProvider provider
(Dropbox/OneDrive/Drive), so one check covers all four. Keep the `.icloud`
sibling test as a fallback for older systems. The hydration nudge needs a
provider-appropriate path too: `brctl download` is iCloud-only and is a no-op
for `~/Library/CloudStorage` paths.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.

title: bind_notebook_okf fails on a path that does not exist yet, so agents must mkdir first
description:
## What

`bind_notebook_okf(notebook_id, path)` over MCP returns

    Not a folder: /Users/.../Alchemy Sync Test/sync-test-dropbox

when the target folder does not exist. The UI verb ("Keep on disk as OKF...")
always hands it a folder the picker created, so this only bites the MCP/CLI
surface — but that surface is the one agents use, and RFC-okf-live.md 5.5
documents `bind_notebook_okf(notebook_id, path)` with no note that the folder
must pre-exist. The tool description does not say so either.

## Repro

    bind_notebook_okf(notebook_id="<id>", path="/some/new/folder")
    -> error "Not a folder: /some/new/folder"
    mkdir -p "/some/new/folder"
    bind_notebook_okf(...)  # succeeds

## Ask

Either create the directory (the seed pass writes into it anyway and 5.5 says
"an empty folder gets the seed pass"), or say so in the tool description so an
agent knows to mkdir.

Found during v0.55.0 cloud-provider QA.

title: iCloud container entitlement for the branded Alchemy folder

Needs the iCloud entitlement in src-tauri/Entitlements.plist, an App ID with iCloud enabled, a Developer ID provisioning profile embedded as Contents/embedded.provisionprofile, and release.sh/notarization changes. Paul: App IDs → com.thrashr888.alchemy → iCloud → Edit → tick iCloud.com.thrashr888.alchemy → Save → Profiles → regenerate 'Alchemy Developer ID iCloud' → download. Then: op document edit, a debug bundle build with tauri.icloud.conf.json to verify launch + container folder, then release.

title: Reader: show a source's cover image in the properties block
description: A cover picked in the gallery (set_source_image / the gallery picker) only shows on the gallery card. The reader's properties block (Type / URL / Added / Size / Tags / Note) should carry the same image as a thumbnail when imageUrl is set and not '-', so the choice is visible where the source is actually read.
close_reason: On cld/mcp-import-feedback, PR #39

title: Dev builds clobber the shared MCP discovery file
description: Dev instances bind mcp_port+1 (41415) to avoid colliding with the installed app, but both write the same <app-data>/mcp.json. A dev run rewrites it to 41415; after the dev app quits, the CLI and agents discover a dead port until the installed app restarts (hit live 2026-08-31: CLI errored against 41415 while nothing listened; installed app relaunch fixed it). Options: dev builds write mcp.dev.json and leave mcp.json alone, or discovery consumers fall back to the default port when the recorded pid is dead. Discovery already records pid.
close_reason: Fixed on main cabac45: dev builds write/remove mcp.dev.json instead of clobbering mcp.json; CLAUDE.md documents ALCHEMY_MCP_DISCOVERY for aiming the CLI at a dev build. Gates green; live run blocked by a concurrent pre-fix dev instance from another worktree (which demonstrated the bug once more).

title: Thread window labels through the remaining meta_step broadcasts
description: PR #29 windowed the Home Chat meta:// events (payload carries the window label; the store self-filters, src/lib/store.ts bindGlobalListeners). The global-tool flows in src-tauri/src/commands.rs (~7863-8042: add_urls_from_home, command routing 'Choosing a notebook'/'Checking for commands') still emit label-less meta_step broadcasts that every window accepts. Thread the asking window's label through those call chains so multi-window Home Chats are fully isolated.
